name.text: Predicting consecutive football match outcomes using tree diagrams

questiontext.text:
{@team@} plays two consecutive matches in the local football league. In each match, the team independently has a probability of \(P(W) = {@str_W@}\) to win, \(P(D) = {@str_D@}\) to draw, and \(P(L) = {@str_L@}\) to lose.

Construct a two-stage tree diagram where each node splits into three branches (W, D, L).

a) Find the probability that the team wins both matches.

(Enter your answer as an exact decimal).

\(P(\text{Win and Win}) =\) [[input:ans1]]

[[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

b) Find the probability that the team draws both matches.

\(P(\text{Draw and Draw}) =\) [[input:ans2]]

[[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

c) Find the probability that the team wins at least one match.

(Hint: It is easier to use the complement rule. First find the probability of winning NO matches, which means getting a Draw or a Loss in both matches).

\(P(\text{At least one Win}) =\) [[input:ans3]]

[[validation:ans3]] [[feedback:prt3]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution:

Because the matches are independent, the branch probabilities remain exactly the same at both levels of the tree diagram.

Part a: Winning Both
To find the probability of a specific sequence, we multiply the probabilities along that path:

\( \displaystyle P(W, W) = P(W) \times P(W) \)

\( \displaystyle P(W, W) = {@str_W@} \times {@str_W@} \)

\( \displaystyle \boxed{ P(\text{Win both}) = {@ta1_str@} } \)

Part b: Drawing Both
Similarly, we multiply the draw probabilities:

\( \displaystyle P(D, D) = P(D) \times P(D) \)

\( \displaystyle P(D, D) = {@str_D@} \times {@str_D@} \)

\( \displaystyle \boxed{ P(\text{Draw both}) = {@ta2_str@} } \)

Part c: Winning At Least One Match
The easiest way to calculate "at least one" is to use the complement of "none". The team wins ZERO matches if they get a Draw or a Loss in both games. The probability of not winning a single match is:

\( \displaystyle P(\text{Not Winning}) = P(D) + P(L) = {@str_D@} + {@str_L@} = {@P_Not_W_str@} \)

The probability of this happening twice in a row is:

\( \displaystyle P(\text{Zero Wins}) = {@P_Not_W_str@} \times {@P_Not_W_str@} = {@P_Zero_Wins_str@} \)

Therefore, the probability of winning at least one match is the complement of winning zero matches:

\( \displaystyle P(\text{At least one Win}) = 1 - P(\text{Zero Wins}) \)

\( \displaystyle P(\text{At least one Win}) = 1 - {@P_Zero_Wins_str@} \)

\( \displaystyle \boxed{ P(\text{At least one Win}) = {@ta3_str@} } \)

The tree diagram has three branches at each stage:

[[jsxgraph width="460px" height="372px"]] (function() { var L1 = [['W', '{#str_W#}'],['D', '{#str_D#}'],['L', '{#str_L#}']], L2 = [[['W', '{#str_W#}'],['D', '{#str_D#}'],['L', '{#str_L#}']],[['W', '{#str_W#}'],['D', '{#str_D#}'],['L', '{#str_L#}']],[['W', '{#str_W#}'],['D', '{#str_D#}'],['L', '{#str_L#}']]], LV = []; var n = 9, wide = LV.length ? 15 : 12; var b = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, {boundingbox:[-0.4, n + 0.4, wide, 0.3], axis:false, grid:false, showNavigation:false, showCopyright:false, pan:{enabled:false}, zoom:{enabled:false}}); function lab(p, q, t, txt) { // t: how far along the branch the label sits // probability label 55% along the branch, above an upward branch and below a downward one var x = p[0] + t*(q[0]-p[0]), y = p[1] + t*(q[1]-p[1]); var off = (q[1] >= p[1]) ? 0.32 : -0.32; b.create('text', [x, y + off, txt], {anchorX:'middle', anchorY:'middle', fontSize:13, fixed:true, strokeColor:'#1565c0'}); } var y = n, k = 0, root = [0, (n + 1)/2]; b.create('point', root, {name:'', size:3, fixed:true, color:'#333', showInfobox:false}); for (var i = 0; i < L1.length; i++) { var m = L2[i].length, ymid = y - (m - 1)/2, p1 = [3.0, ymid]; b.create('segment', [root, p1], {strokeColor:'#555', fixed:true}); lab(root, p1, 0.55, L1[i][1]); b.create('text', [3.15, ymid, L1[i][0]], {anchorY:'middle', fontSize:15, fixed:true}); for (var j = 0; j < m; j++) { var s2 = [6.3, ymid], p2 = [9.2, y]; b.create('segment', [s2, p2], {strokeColor:'#555', fixed:true}); lab(s2, p2, 0.72, L2[i][j][1]); b.create('text', [9.35, y, L2[i][j][0]], {anchorY:'middle', fontSize:15, fixed:true}); if (LV.length) b.create('text', [12.0, y, LV[k]], {anchorY:'middle', fontSize:13, fixed:true, strokeColor:'#2e7d32'}); y -= 1; k++; } } })(); [[/jsxgraph]]

questiondescription.text:
This question is based on the tree-diagram examples (two independent stages) in the section Tree Diagrams of the CBC Grade 11 Mathematics textbook (INNODEMS).

Three-Branch Tree Diagram: Independent Events

node.description: Check if they added instead of multiplied

truefeedback.text: You added the probability of winning to itself. When moving along the branches of a tree diagram for consecutive independent events, you must multiply the probabilities.

falsefeedback.text: Incorrect. The probability of winning both matches is \(P(W) \times P(W)\).
Incorrect. The probability of drawing both matches is \(P(D) \times P(D)\).

truefeedback.text: Excellent. You correctly used the complement of winning zero matches.

You calculated \(1 - P(\text{Winning Both})\). That calculation gives you the probability of winning at most one match (i.e. not winning both). To find the probability of winning at least one match, you must subtract the probability of winning ZERO matches from 1.

falsefeedback.text: Incorrect. Find the probability of winning no matches at all (meaning getting a Draw or Loss in both games), and subtract that result from 1.
